Svalyava Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakarpatska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Jews began arriving in Svalyava in the 18th century, with 45 settlers by 1830; the population reached 319 (19.2 percent) by 1880 and 1,099 by 1921, engaged as tradesmen, artisans, doctors, and one pharmacist, with Jews owning seven factories and a bank. Following the March 1939 Hungarian occupation, Jews were persecuted and forced out of their occupations; by 1941, the population reached 1,423 (16.9 percent), with 150 drafted into forced labor battalions the previous year. In August 1941, Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to German-occupied Kamianets-Podilskyi and shot; about 1,000 remaining Jews of Svalyava were deported to Auschwitz on May 22, 1944.
